sources.entry: Gifski - Convert videos to high-quality GIFs. ![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/no/app/gifski/id1351639930?platform=mac)

summary.one_liner: A macOS app that converts video files into high-quality animated GIFs, built on the gifski encoder.
summary.what_it_does: Gifski is a Mac app wrapping the gifski encoder, which uses pngquant techniques for cross-frame palettes and temporal dithering to produce GIFs with thousands of colors per frame at up to 50 FPS. A "Quality" slider allows smaller, lower-quality output via gifsicle. It accepts any video format macOS can read, such as MP4 or MOV with H264, HEVC, or ProRes, but not QuickTime Animation or WebM. Settings include dimensions, speed, frame rate, quality, cropping, and looping. It also offers a bounce (yo-yo) option that plays forward and then backward, doubling the frame count. Conversion is available through a share extension, a Services menu item, and a Finder Quick Action shortcut, and keyboard shortcuts let you copy or save the result.
use_cases: Convert a screen recording into a GIF
Make animated GIFs for design work or Dribbble posts
Turn an MP4 or MOV clip into a looping GIF
Batch-convert videos from Finder or Shortcuts
Create small, lower-quality GIFs for the web
Build a GIF from a PNG sequence via FFmpeg
how_to_run: Download Gifski from the Mac App Store, or use the non-App Store build linked in the README
Open a video in Gifski or share it to Gifski from any app's Share menu
To build from source: install Rust, run brew install SwiftLint, run xcode-select --install, then build in Xcode
notable: Cross-frame palettes and temporal dithering for high-color GIFs up to 50 FPS
Share extension, Services menu item, and Finder Quick Action shortcut
Non-App Store build for users who cannot access the App Store
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later; older versions are available for macOS 10.13 through 13
The non-App Store version does not receive automatic updates and is updated once a year
GIF files can be very large, and the app works best with short clips
Frame rates above 50 FPS are not supported; no WebM support; Windows and Linux are not supported
